thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager opened — high tail latency observed for hosted inference in us-west1. Incident ID INC-2026-244. Paging oncall.

anna_oncall: saw a spike ~03:44 UTC, ~20% of requests > 5s and a few 504s. Noting customer-facing 99th latency jump. Escalating.

luis_support: ACME reported timeouts in their production app, they started seeing errors at ~03:43 UTC. Ticket #SUP-809 attached.

mike_infra: looking at autoscaler and GPU pool, no obvious node OOMs. CPU on control-plane is fine. Will pull serving logs and qps graphs.

henry_runtime: I merged a small runtime kernel selection change in the last release (sha abc1234) that tightens kernel selection heuristics for mixed-precision paths. It landed last night, could be related.

sophia_sre: ok, hypothesis tracking in-thread:
1) regression from runtime kernel selection change (henry)
2) traffic pattern + batching causing KV cache thrash
3) infra/networking blip (less likely)

anna_oncall: Let's do quick scoped mitigations:
- Disable the new kernel selection flag on a canary host pool
- Temporarily widen autoscaler concurrency cutoff to avoid batching delay
- Revert runtime change if we confirm regression
Owners: henry (runtime revert), mike (infra scaling), anna (coord).

henry_runtime: running a canary revert now on one host pool to validate. Command I used:
```bash
deploy runtime --pool us-west1-canary --image sha=abc1233 --env RUNTIME_KERNSEL=legacy
```
I'll report when done.

deploy-bot: Revert deployment started by henry_runtime (us-west1-canary) — roll to sha abc1233. Rolling update in progress.

mike_infra: I bumped autoscaler thresholds to allow +30% capacity headroom and disabled aggressive continuous batching for the affected pool:
```yaml
autoscaler:
  scale_up: 1.3
batching:
  continuous: false
```
Watching metrics.

anna_oncall: luis, can you confirm ACME still seeing errors after these changes?

luis_support: pinged ACME; they report degraded but improved response times. Still occasional 5s tails.

deploy-bot: Revert deployment completed on us-west1-canary — all pods rolled to abc1233.

henry_runtime: canary metrics look better — 99th latency down ~60% on the canary pool.

sophia_sre: good signal. Next: do a controlled revert to a subset of production pools (not full global) — plan: revert 2/6 serving pools, monitor 15m, then expand. henry to own.

henry_runtime: starting partial revert: pools p2 and p4. Command: `deploy runtime --pools p2,p4 --image sha=abc1233 --reason revert-test`

deploy-bot: Partial revert to pools p2,p4 initiated by henry_runtime. ETA 6m.

anna_oncall: I'll update incident timeline note:
- 03:43 UTC initial customer reports (ACME)
- 03:44 UTC alert triggered on 99th latency
- 03:46 UTC oncall paged (anna)
- 03:50 UTC identified recent runtime kernel change as top suspect
- 03:55 UTC canary revert started
- 04:01 UTC canary revert succeeded with improved latencies
- 04:08 UTC partial revert started (p2,p4)

mike_infra: also checked top-of-stack network errors — minimal packet drops, no route flaps. So infra blip unlikely.

luis_support: ACME confirms p2/p4 path shows improvements; overall error rate reduced ~75% but some customers on other pools still see tails.

henry_runtime: after p2/p4 revert, 99th dropped across the region by ~45%. I'm going to open a revert PR for the kernel selection change and tag it for postmortem. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/512

sophia_sre: hypothesis status:
- H1 (runtime change) — supported by canary + partial revert metrics (likely cause).
- H2 (KV cache thrash) — still possible as an amplifier; need heap and KV metrics for affected hosts.
- H3 (network) — unlikely.

anna_oncall: action items:
- henry: complete staged revert to remaining pools (owner) and open revert PR (in progress).
- mike: keep autoscaler headroom and batching disabled until we validate (owner).
- sophia: collect heap/KV cache metrics and summarize in timeline (owner).
- luis: keep ACME updated and collect any request traces they can share.

henry_runtime: starting staged revert to remaining pools now (p1,p3,p5,p6). Will pause if regressions seen.

deploy-bot: Staged revert in progress — rolling through p1,p3,p5,p6.

sophia_sre: attaching quick log excerpts (truncated) — searching for cache errors and token loopbacks:
```
[us-west1/pool p3] runtime ERROR kv_cache: eviction_pressure=0.92, miss_rate=0.78, in_flight_requests=2048
[us-west1/pool p3] trace id=xyz request_id=abc status=504 latency_ms=5203
```
These lines align with high miss rate hypothesis.

anna_oncall: good catch. If KV miss_rate is that high, batching + kernel change could amplify slow paths. Sophia, add that to the RCA notes.

luis_support: ACME reports full recovery for their traffic path after the staged revert completed. They will keep us posted for 2 hours.

mike_infra: I'll keep autoscaler and batching flags as-is for now. We should schedule a rollback window for the original runtime change once we confirm fixes.

henry_runtime: Revert complete across pools. Rolling metrics show region-wide 99th back to normal. I submitted the revert PR and flagged it urgent.

sophia_sre: next steps for in-incident RCA:
- gather full heap and KV cache metrics for the affected window (03:30–04:15 UTC) — attach logs and graphs
- run a replay of sampled requests in canary with the original kernel change to reproduce
- correlate request shapes that triggered high miss rates

anna_oncall: I'll convert this thread into an incident postmortem template and assign owners for each section. Closing pager once ACME confirms stable for 2 hours.

eva_pm: notify CSM and schedule a customer follow-up call to explain root cause and mitigation.

sophia_sre: quick note: label hypotheses as final in postmortem: root cause = regression introduced by kernel selection change causing slower kernel path and amplifying KV cache miss thrash under real traffic patterns. Secondary contributor = continuous batching config.

anna_oncall: thanks team. I'll update the incident tracker and mark this thread for RCA drafting. :white_check_mark:
